manufacturer_data.description: Match on the bytes 88 EC at payload offset 0 or 1 — a leading version byte makes hosts report 0x88XX instead of 0xEC88 (= 60552). goodsType (2 bytes BE after the company bytes) distinguishes BLE-first models: e.g. 57=H6071, 67=H6075, 188=H60A0, 6=H6118/H6194, 12=H6179, 36=H7040; WiFi-first models carry generic values there and are named by the local name instead.

The app's broadcast parser requires the bytes 88 EC in the manufacturer-specific AD structure, with a 2-byte big-endian goodsType after them — but a leading version byte (low nibble = broadcast version) can shift the company bytes to payload offset 1, so host stacks report the "company id" as 0x88XX (0x8802, 0x8803, 0x8843 observed on Govee WiFi lights 2026-08-22) instead of 0xEC88. Match on 88 EC at offset 0 or 1. Whether the 128-bit service UUID is present in the ADV packet varies by model and is unverified for most of the family (the 2026-08-22 WiFi-light sample advertised none).

device.name: Govee RGB Lights (classic, non-segmented)
device.notes:
Govee's plain-RGB light family: bulbs (H6071/H6075/H6085/H6086/H6089, H60A0), RGB (non-IC) strips (H6110, H614B/H614E, H6159, H6160, H6178), car lights (H6114, H6118, H6194) and assorted older strips. All of them speak the shared Govee 20-byte BLE protocol on service 00010203-0405-0607-0809-0a0b0c0d1910, characteristic …2b11 (write and notify on the same characteristic; CCCD 0x2902).
FRAME: 20 bytes fixed. [0]=0x33 control / 0xAA query, [1]=command, [2..18]=payload zero-padded, [19]=XOR of bytes 0-18. Write ACKs echo the command id with payload byte 0 = 0 on success. The app sends keep-alive AA 01 every ~2 s while connected, and after connecting reads state with AA 01 (power), AA 04 (brightness), AA 05 (mode).
WHAT "CLASSIC" MEANS HERE: color is whole-device only — 33 05 02 R G B. There are no per-segment commands and no Kelvin on the wire: white / color-temperature requests are sent as 33 05 02 FF FF FF 01 Wr Wg Wb where the shade triple comes from the vendor's fixed Kelvin→RGB table (app range 1000-10000 K). Scenes are 33 05 04 <id_lo> <id_hi> (16-bit little-endian; built-ins include 1=sunset, 4=movie, 8=blinking, 9=candlelight, 10=breath, 15=snow). Music mode is the legacy 33 05 11 form (effect 16=energy / 17=rhythm / 18=spectrum / 19=scroll, then a sensitivity byte; rhythm and later effects add a dynamic flag, a fixed-color flag and an RGB triple). DIY apply is 33 05 0A <code_lo> <code_hi> (code 0x00FE = "just uploaded"). Several of these SKUs also exist in the app's RGBIC modules — when a unit reports segment support it answers the extended commands in govee-rgbic-light.yaml instead; treat that spec as the superset.
WIFI VARIANTS: many family members (H6085/H6086/H6089 bulbs, H61xx strips) are WiFi+BLE. BLE local control works with no WiFi and no cloud. WiFi provisioning is a BLE write (see govee-rgbic-light.yaml, which documents the shared provisioning frame); the bulbs additionally fall back to a softAP (`Govee_bulb_<sku>`) hosting a TCP provisioning socket on 192.168.1.1:7200. Some firmware exposes Govee's local Wi-Fi (LAN) API once enabled in the app — the toggle is a BLE-protocol frame (write type 0xE3, sub 0x01, payload 0x01) and the LAN protocol itself is firmware-side (see helpful_urls).
CONFIDENCE: HIGH for framing, UUIDs and the core command set (app-confirmed and corroborated by independent RE); MEDIUM for the per-model variant list (module routing in the app, not hardware-verified per model) and LOW for advertised-name forms (GVH<sku>… is the modern form, ihoment_H<sku>_<hex> the legacy one, Minger rebadges exist).

credentials.notes: On WiFi models the SSID/passphrase travels over the (unbonded) BLE link inside the provisioning frame — plaintext at the application layer, so anyone in range during onboarding could observe it. BLE-only models exchange no credentials. The optional 8-byte BLE auth key (AA B1 / 33 B2) is static per device.

factory_reset.description: Not recovered from the app per model. The near-universal pattern for mains-powered Govee lights is rapid power cycling; WiFi models additionally have an in-app "restore factory settings" path. The signal that a power-cycle reset took is a self-initiated blink and re-advertising as unprovisioned; if the light simply comes back on unchanged, the toggle count was wrong for that generation.
factory_reset.effect: Clears WiFi credentials and cloud binding (WiFi models) and returns the light to factory defaults.

procedures.basis: Generic pattern for mains-powered smart lights, consistent with Govee's published help text. Not confirmed per model.
procedures.description: Switch the light off and on at the wall in quick succession, about a second in each state, watching for a self-initiated blink at the end.
procedures.indicator: Light blinks by itself, then re-advertises as unprovisioned.
procedures.name: Power cycle

steps.action: Toggle power rapidly 5 times, roughly one second on and one second off.
steps.expect: Light blinks to confirm reset and re-advertises. If it just comes back on unchanged, try three cycles instead.

methods.description: No provisioning needed for BLE control. Power on, scan, connect, write. WiFi onboarding is optional and only needed for cloud / LAN-API use.

steps.action: Power the light and scan for BLE advertisements.
Connect and write control commands to …2b11.

setup.notes: No BLE pairing/bonding for local control. A minority of units demand an application-layer key exchange: AA B1 reads an 8-byte per-device key (some models only return the real key while the physical button is held, as on the H5080 plug family), and the connection then authenticates once with 33 B2 <key>. Most lights in this family skip auth entirely. Newer firmware may instead require the AES session handshake documented in govee-rgbic-light.yaml — the device announces this through the BGC-info characteristic, so a client discovers it rather than guessing.

rejoin.notes: BLE control needs no rejoin. WiFi models rejoin the WLAN via the app's BLE provisioning write; BLE remains usable throughout.

apply_diy.description: Apply a stored DIY effect. Packet: [0x33, 0x05, 0x0A, <code_lo>, <code_hi>, 0x00*14, <xor>]; code 0x00FE activates the most recently uploaded DIY payload.

checksum.description: XOR of the preceding 19 frame bytes; encoder-filled, never a control.

get_brightness.description: Query brightness; response payload byte 0 = 0-100. Packet: [0xAA, 0x04, 0x00*17, <xor>]

get_mode.description: Query current mode; response payload byte 0 = sub-mode (0x02 color, 0x04 scene, 0x0A diy, 0x11 music), remainder = sub-mode state (for color: RGB at payload 1-3). Packet: [0xAA, 0x05, 0x00*17, <xor>]

keep_alive.description: Connection keep-alive, every ~2 s. Packet: [0xAA, 0x01, 0x00*17, 0xAB]. Doubles as the power-state query: response payload byte 0 = power, byte 1 carries battery/charge bits on battery models.

brightness.notes: Percent. (The older H6001 legacy-bulb path is the exception: it takes a raw 0-255 wire value — see govee-h6001-bulb.yaml.)

checksum.description: XOR of the preceding 19 frame bytes; encoder-filled, never a control.
XOR of the preceding 19 frame bytes; encoder-filled, never a control.

set_color_white.description: White / color temperature via the vendor's fixed Kelvin→RGB shade table (no Kelvin value crosses the link on this family). Packet: [0x33, 0x05, 0x02, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0x01, <shade R>, <shade G>, <shade B>, 0x00*9, <xor>]. A color+white mix form also exists: [0x33, 0x05, 0x02, R1, G1, B1, 0x01, R2, G2, B2, …].

checksum.description: XOR of the preceding 19 frame bytes; encoder-filled, never a control.

set_music_mode.description: Legacy music mode (sub-mode 0x11). Packet: [0x33, 0x05, 0x11, <effect>, <sensitivity>, …]. Effects: 16=energy (payload ends after sensitivity), 17=rhythm, 18=spectrum, 19=scroll — the latter three add [dynamic, colorFlag, R, G, B] where colorFlag 0 = use the fixed RGB that follows, 1 = auto color.

checksum.description: XOR of the preceding 19 frame bytes; encoder-filled, never a control.

set_scene.description: Apply a built-in scene. Packet: [0x33, 0x05, 0x04, <id_lo>, <id_hi>, 0x00*14, <xor>]. Built-in ids seen in the app: 1=sunset, 4=movie, 5=date, 7=romantic, 8=blinking, 9=candlelight, 10=breath, 15=snow, 16=dynamic, 21=chase, 22=stream.

characteristics.name: Control Write/Notify
characteristics.notes: All control and query traffic. Keep-alive AA 01 00..00 AB every ~2 s while connected (skipped while a multi-packet transfer is in flight).

services.name: Govee Light Command Service
services.notes: The shared Govee command profile. Commands are 20-byte fixed packets, byte 19 = XOR of bytes 0-18. The same characteristic is write and notify: write ACKs echo the command id (payload byte 0 = 0 = OK) and query responses arrive as notifications. Unsolicited 0xEE-notify frames report async events (e.g. sub 0x11 = WiFi connect status, 0x40 = device status report); family 0x30 detail notifies cover light status (sub 1), battery (sub 3), music (sub 4).
